title: ‘He’s a warrior’ | Penn State QB Alex Manske impresses early at fall camp after returning from injury
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
During the second practice of fall camp, Alex Manske stepped up in the pocket to unleash a deep ball to the front left corner of the end zone. It sailed over the defender, who was pressing hard in man coverage, and dropped perfectly into Zay Robinson’s outstretched arms for a touchdown.

This was one of the instances when Penn State knew their young quarterback was back and better than ever.

“Zay is my guy, so when I had him one on one, I knew I wanted to throw it to him,” Manske said at local media day. “Being able to throw the ball down the field and connect — it was definitely, ‘I'm back.’”

Until the start of fall camp this week, Manske had been dealing with an undisclosed injury that kept him off the gridiron entirely.

Matt Campbell announced that Manske was fully cleared to play at the Big Ten Media Days in Chicago at the end of July, and having him back has greatly increased the depth and competition level of the quarterback room.

At local media day on Friday, the team had high praise for Manske’s return to form, his mental fortitude and his love for football in general. Campbell also spoke highly of his recent practice performances.

“He's playing as good as football in the last two days as we've witnessed Alex Manske playing his entire career,” Campbell said. “He certainly is an elite athlete. He's a guy that could probably start at safety, and he's a guy that's got the ability from a mental capacity.”

This wasn’t the first time Manske missed a spring and summer camp. Last year, he was dealing with a torn ulnar collateral ligament in his elbow, dubbed the “Brock Purdy injury” by Campbell.

For this year’s spring ball, Manske was still back in Iowa and had to tune into meetings on Zoom and watch practice film remotely. In June, the former Cyclone was throwing with his quarterback trainer in Iowa to rebuild his strength and confidence.

“Not being able to throw for a while, I almost feel like it kind of helped me reset my mechanics,” Manske said. “I think it's really helped me be more confident in my ability and just my throwing hands and things. I feel about as good as I ever have right now.”

During the recovery process, Manske had the support of his fellow quarterback Iowa State transfer Rocco Becht, who kept up with his young apprentice with frequent text messages ranging from check-ins to answering film questions.

Campbell, Taylor Mouser and quarterbacks coach Jake Waters were also vital resources for Manske. The message to Manske from the coaching staff was for him to recover at his own pace and to stay positive despite the adversity.

Waters specifically stressed going “slow and right.”

“That guy loves football so much,” Waters said. “It was hard on him being away and not being around, but he just wanted to stay involved and I was constantly on the phone with him and talking through stuff. That was probably the hardest part because he just loves it, loves being around the guys, loves meeting the team, loves to compete.”

Now back at full strength, Manske has traded second-string reps back-and-forth with Christopher Newport transfer Connor Barry, but the redshirt freshman who Campbell believed was the “quarterback of the future” at Iowa State has undoubtedly shined in his return to the gridiron.

“He's a warrior, he's a fighter, and so I'm just excited for him to be back and have more competition in the room,” Becht said. "It's good to have guys in the room that are able to go out there and make plays because you never know what may happen during a season.”

title: ‘Super beneficial for football IQ’ | Penn State LB Caleb Bacon experimenting move to edge in fall camp
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State linebackers are no stranger to moving to the defensive line over the past couple of years.

Former edge rusher Abdul Carter made the switch following his sophomore season, while current defensive end LaVar Arrington II recently made the switch. Now, linebacker Caleb Bacon is testing the waters of a change to defensive end, something he has a little familiarity with.

“He's a smart football player, and we felt like we gave him so many reps in the spring at linebacker,” Matt Campbell said at local media day. “We'd be missing the boat not to start him off in fall camp on the edge. I think (Bacon) is kind of one of those multiplicity pieces.”

Bacon’s capability to move down to the defensive line provides added depth to both position rooms, where he could line up on the edge or drop back in coverage as a linebacker and still make an impact.

The Iowa native moved down to the edge on occasion at Iowa State, but never was in a spot where could stay down there due to the 3-3-5 look the Cyclones deployed on defense. Now, Bacon has more opportunities to move to defensive line, already surprising the coaching staff through just two days of fall practice.

“I think we've been really pleasantly surprised just how well he's looked up on the line of scrimmage,” Campbell said. “So I think he just gives us another piece that we can do a lot of different things with him.”

The defensive coaching staff wants to get the most of its entire unit, using a multitude of players at different positions, and if Bacon can provide that no matter what position he slots in at, he’s going to see a lot of playing time.

“I've seen a guy that loves football and is a good team player,” edge rushers coach Christian Smith said. “So he's going to do whatever he can to help his team and get on the field.”

It’s not just any player that can take on this type of role, having to rely on previous practice at linebacker while working out on the edge to start fall practice. Bacon’s IQ has stood off the charts to his coaches, and he understands the benefit of knowing both positions to expand that even more.

Bacon had a conversation with Arrington recently to discuss the change, as Arrington made the change almost immediately after Campbell was hired. Arrington noted the “thought process” and the ability to “play more freely and kind of let the game come to him,” as advantages to moving to edge rusher during the conversation.

Bacon does recognize the physicality adjustments needed to fully switch to edge rusher, but his selflessness to do what’s best for the team has given him the task of slowly transitioning during fall camp.

“I think just really whatever you know this team needs,” Bacon said. “If we need edge rushers, if we need linebackers, I think I'm really just ready for whatever. Kind of knowing this scheme of it all really helps.”

title: Penn State notebook | Matt Campbell talks processes, depth chart preparation
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
For the first time since Blue-White Practice, Matt Campbell took the podium in Happy Valley as reporters gathered for local media day on Friday.

Among the topics of conversation were the team’s final journey with less than a month until the season, continued battles for a starting role and the development of a winning culture.

Here’s what Campbell had to say with 29 days until kickoff against Marshall.

Preparation for the journey

Over the last eight months, Campbell has described practice as “habits in the winter” and “developing a team in the spring.” On Thursday, he called the final eight-week window the “preparation for the journey” with 29 days until the opening kickoff.

“It’s how do you create the journey, the habits, the mentality, that’s going to allow you to weather the storm of college football and the storm you’re in now?” Campbell said. “You’re going to have tough days. We don’t know when they’re coming, but it’s coming.”

For the players who are returning from last year’s let-down season, they’ve experienced the lows of college football. Now, the entire team is working to build those habits and practices to correct the issues before they become a problem.

“How does Penn State not beat Penn State? That’s the starting point for a football team and understanding how to go into a football game and not beat ourselves,” Campbell said. “That’s easier said than done, and I think we’ve all been a part of that in college football.”

As his team has taken the field for practice throughout the summer and during the last two days of fall camp, Campbell’s turned to his players for leadership.

Campbell stressed the importance of players supporting each other and helping each other, saying “when I keep saying it, they shut me off really fast, but when the players demand it, powerful things have an opportunity to happen.”

Depth chart

This year all players are in an “earn it position,” as this is a brand new Penn State squad with players from all over the country coming together into one team.

“You have to earn it because there’s enough good depth,” Campbell said. “There’s enough good players that they’re pushing for playing, and I think that’s probably one of the real positives that I’ve seen through the summer and the early part of fall camp.”

While Campbell will roll out his starting lineup for Week 1 against Marshall, he expects his squad to cycle through players week in and week out. Positions like running back, wide receiver and tight end have enough depth to see the second and third string take meaningful snaps.

Campbell discussed the team’s ability to play 12 or 13-man personnel with Benjamin Brahamer, Andrew Rappleyea and Gabe Burkle all playing big roles at the tight end spot.

“I’ve always felt like the more guys that can have a role on your football team, the healthier your football team is,” Campbell said.

While some starting roles are a lot more secure than others, positions like left tackle, center and defensive line are among the biggest battles.

Tackles Malachi Goodman, Garrett Sexton and Owen Alicienne have received praise throughout the offseason, including from Campbell on Friday, as he called Goodman “one of the best humans he met since he’s been here,” while applauding Sexton and Aliciene’s growth.

“Physically, (Sexton) looks as good as I’ve ever seen him,” Campbell said. “He shows some of the similar flashes for a really young, talented player.”

Winning culture

Campbell said the thing he enjoys most about coaching is getting to lead a group of young men and help them in their development as people. With that mindset comes a necessity for culture, something he values greatly.

“I think the biggest thing is as you’re building the foundation of the culture, what are the standards and expectations that we are going to live by?” Campbell said. “Aligning and unifying everybody in the program to that value system, I think that’s been really rewarding.”

With culture development comes creating a winning mindset. Some programs pride themselves being winning-focused, but Campbell takes the passive approach.

“How we live inside of our walls, how we build the right culture inside of our walls, that's going to build the foundation of a football program moving forward,” Campbell said.

Over the last eight months, the Nittany Lions have brought together a group of Penn State returners, Iowa State transfers, freshmen and additional transfers.

Through the process, the team has meshed together and built a culture of winning amongst the over 100 athletes and dozens of coaches.

“I think the growth we’ve made in six months understanding those value systems and my whole belief process goes back to how you do everything,” Campbell said. “It is all leading to being your best on those 12 guaranteed Saturdays, and I think everything that the program is about is we’re trying to win on Saturdays.”

title: Practice observations | QBs showcase deep ball in Penn State's second fall practice
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Chase Sowell lined up back-to-back against safety Ibn McDaniels, and when the signal came, the pair circled the cones opposite to each other. Sowell sprinted up the field, narrowly avoiding McDaniels’ grasp before the next two players entered the drill.

The Nittany Lions just barely beat the heavy State College rainfall for their second fall camp practice under Matt Campbell. Although the downpour stopped, the skies remained gloomy as light mist came and went.

Before breaking off into position groups, the team came together for a dynamic warmup and stretch. There were two NFL scouts in attendance for the San Francisco 49ers and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The quarterbacks worked on their decision-making between scrambling or stepping up in the pocket to make a throw, and the running backs got to showcase their agility and ball security. Meanwhile, the defensive line worked on getting under their opposition, and the edge rushers practiced blocking kicks.

Quarterback Alex Manske returned to practice on Wednesday and continued to work in with Connor Barry for second and third-string reps. Campbell said during the Big Ten Media Days that Manske was fully cleared to return for fall camp, and he appeared to have not missed a beat.

A few players had either leg sleeves or braces on, including linebacker Tony Rojas, who had a sleeve on his left leg, tight end Andrew Rappleyea with a right leg sleeve and wide receiver Peter Gonzalez with a right leg brace.

Regardless, all three were full participants in the practice, with Gonzalez putting on an impressive showing throughout the session. He had a leaping catch later in practice that drew a host of cheers from the offensive sideline.

Logan Cunningham was another depth receiver to have some big moments, most notably an over-the-shoulder diving reception on a slant route in 7-on-7 action after which he tumbled out of bounds.

The biggest moment of the practice, however, came from the starters. In the heat of the 7-on-7 period, Rocco Becht and Brett Eskildsen combined to beat the defense’s man coverage with a deep strike, threading the needle for Eskildsen to toe-tap the sideline for the catch.

Two plays later, the backups were feeling it too, as Manske and Zay Robinson linked up on a similar corner route for a touchdown.

Both plays set off thunderous uproars, with the entire offensive unit swarming the receivers while the defenders set up for the next play. Campbell smiled as the team celebrated.

However, the practice wasn’t perfect, as is expected early in fall camp.

In for safety Jeremiah Cooper was Jamison Patton, and he had a miscommunication with Audavion Collins during routes. Patton was calling out to Collins to watch Koby Howard on an out route, but Collins instead ran to the inside, allowing Howard to make an uncontested catch with room for additional yardage up the sideline.

There were also a few drops and stumbles throughout the practice that resulted in push-ups, as seen when Sowell dropped a ball on a wide-open dig route.

Tight end Gabe Burkle, who was spotted with his jersey on but without his helmet, didn’t participate during practice. On the other side of the ball, Cooper and linebacker Alex Tatsch were seen working on their own off to the side in rehab drills.

title: How former Penn State players are performing in NFL training camp
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State just reported to fall camp on Tuesday, and a new group of former Penn Staters have begun their first training camp in the NFL. Others are entering yet another year of camp before the start of the season.

Here’s training camp news and standouts from former Nittany Lions.

Drew Allar

Drew Allar made headlines during rookie minicamp in the spring when it was made known that new Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy would be starting with Allar from scratch.

McCarthy has seemingly taken Allar under his wing, having been seen coaching him one-on-one, showing that there’s belief Allar could become a starter at some point in his career.

That’s been evident in the early parts of Steelers training camp, as Allar has made impressive passes and plays day in and day out. The consistency is the biggest factor for Allar, who’s already showed off his cannon of an arm. He’s also shown he can place the ball well as he continues improving his footwork.

While Allar likely won’t see any playing time in the regular season, barring injury from Aaron Rodgers, he’s expected to get significant minutes in the preseason as the backup battle continues with Will Howard.

Nick Singleton

Another rookie, Nick Singleton was seen Tuesday getting a handoff from Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward. While that on the surface doesn’t seem meaningful, it shows Singleton is receiving first-team reps.

The Titans used a fifth-round pick on Singleton in the 2026 NFL Draft, and with one of the worst rushing attacks in the NFL last year, the former Penn State standout could add a spark to the run game.

Singleton will be in battle with Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears for playing time, but if the rookie shows the burst that he showed across his career at Penn State, he could quickly move ahead of them.

Joey Porter Jr.

Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. isn’t exactly holding out while he works to get a contract extension with the Steelers, as he’s been present at training camp while also dealing with a back injury.

Porter has turned himself into a bonafide top cornerback in the league, and with recent contract extensions from other cornerbacks in his draft class, he could earn big money from the Steelers.

Pittsburgh hasn’t made any reported progress on an extension with the former Penn Stater, but hold-ins have been a common practice among Steeler players looking for an extension, and all have earned them in prior years.

Nittany Lions on new teams

Multiple former Nittany Lions are making their training camp debut on new rosters ahead of the 2026 season. Edge rusher Odafe Oweh, safety Jaquan Brisker and wide receiver Jahan Dotson are among the names donning new jerseys.

Oweh has opened eyes at training camp with the Washington Commanders after signing a four-year, $100 million deal with the Commanders in March. His speed off the edge has caused immediate issues for Washington’s top offensive unit.

Brisker returned to his home city of Pittsburgh to man the backline of the Steelers’ defense. With many questions in the safety room, Brisker has provided consistent play in practice and is set to be one of the starters, potentially alongside Jalen Ramsey.

Dotson is on his third team, now with the Atlanta Falcons, and has quickly grown a connection with quarterback Michael Penix Jr. In a receiving core that features Drake London and Kyle Pitts, Dotson is likely to have a lot of one-on-one opportunities to make an impact on the Falcons.

Tight ends

Penn State has inserted its name in the “Tight End U” conversation, and the tight ends are continuing to show why in training camp.

Tyler Warren is making spectacular catch after spectacular catch in Indianapolis. Warren finished fifth in receiving yards with 817 among tight ends in his rookie year despite his usage significantly dropping when Daniel Jones went down with an injury. Warren could be in for another big year with his quarterback back to full health ahead of the season.

Pat Freiermuth once again looks to be one of Rodgers’ favorite targets, and with a revamped offense, the former Nittany Lion could be in for a big year. In offenses with Rodgers and McCarthy, the tight end was a significant part of the gameplan, and Freiermuth’s ability to work the middle of the field has already shown in training camp.

Brenton Strange is entering training camp with a new contract. The tight end earned a three-year, $48 million deal after a strong 2025 campaign and became one of Trevor Lawrence’s most reliable targets. Theo Johnson, on the other hand, has struggled to hold onto the ball in training camp in a year where he could see less time with the addition of Isaiah Likely on the New York Giants.

title: 6 viral recipes to try before summer ends
author: Colleen Cratty | For The Collegian
description:
August is upon us, meaning there’s only a few weeks left to enjoy the warm weather. It’s the perfect time to try out some new recipes and soak in those summer vibes.

Whether you’re hosting a barbecue, packing a beach picnic or just looking for a fun meal to make at home, here are six viral recipes to try.

Grillo’s Pickle Dip

This recipe is sure to indulge those with a savory tooth, with its creamy and crunchy mixture of pickles and cream cheese.

With the addition of ranch powder seasoning and crumbled bacon, this dip is a great appetizer paired with some plain potato chips or crackers.

If you’re into spicy food, you can use Grillo’s hot spears and add jalapeños for an extra kick.

This recipe is easy to make, it just requires chopping pickles into a bowl to mix them with some other ingredients. Grillo’s even recommends serving it in the pickle container, so it's perfect for those who like to reuse or college students on a budget. It also travels well, making it a great snack to bring to a cookout!

Trader Joe’s sandwich

This viral recipe is a classic for a lover of Trader Joe’s, a trip to the beach or a quick lunch between summer jobs.

This sandwich uses sun-dried tomato focaccia, the perfect way to inject summer energy into a simple sandwich. The sandwich has turkey, greens, tomatoes, mayonnaise and pesto, creating a fresh and foolproof summer sandwich. You could also remove the turkey for a vegetarian twist.

However you choose to make it, it’s a great choice for a sunny day.

Crispy pasta salad

Pasta salad is a staple when it comes to summer activities, like a picnic or barbecue. But this one puts a special spin on the classic!

Instead of just boiling the pasta, this recipe encourages you to air fry it after, with olive oil and seasoning to create a nice crunch. The crispy pasta is also paired with fresh produce like romaine, cherry tomatoes, red onion and cucumber, as well as feta cheese. The feta brings a tangy flavor, and it can easily be substituted with a vegan version for those avoiding dairy.

Baked feta pasta

This recipe has done numbers on social media and is often called the “TikTok pasta.”

It's super easy to make when you just want to throw something in the oven. All you have to do is put some chopped garlic, a chopped shallot, a block of feta cheese and some grape tomatoes in a casserole dish and bake it. Boil some bowtie pasta, mix up the sauce and now you’ve got a delicious summer pasta.

Most recipes recommend adding in some crushed red pepper flakes for a nice kick to balance out the tangy sauce.

Crunchy cucumber salad

This cucumber salad is a tasty and easy snack for the beach or a perfect side dish for a barbecue.

For the salad, chop up some cucumber and toss it in a dressing. You could use a pre-made italian dressing, make one with olive oil and red wine vinegar or add some sesame oil, ginger and chili crisp for an Asian-inspired dressing.

Some people also like to add sliced onions, avocado or sesame seeds for a variety in texture. Since it only takes a few minutes to prepare, it’s an easy recipe to throw together whenever you need a refreshing snack or side dish.

Fluffy seagull iced latte

This is a great summer drink option, inspired by a viral latte made by the Cape Cod coffee shop, Lighthouse Keepers.

Make a latte with your favorite espresso and choice of milk in a glass lined with marshmallow fluff and peanut butter, and you’ve got a Fluffy Seagull. You can also make a marshmallow cold foam with fluff, heavy cream and milk to top off the drink.

This latte is easy to make and a delicious way to get in some much-needed caffeine in the morning.

title: On ‘one little, tiny rock,’ astronomers have split from astrology
author: Allison Shanley | For The Collegian
description:
It’s become an increasingly common practice to ask for someone’s zodiac sign, whether it be in search of compatibility or a result of mere curiosity. It’s displayed on dating profiles, inked on the pages of newspapers, sold as keychains at gift shops.

Before these modern trends, astrology had a reputable place in scholarly traditions, with astronomy and astrology originally seen as two sides of the same coin. But throughout astronomy’s scientific revolution, research resulted in crossroads between astrologers and astronomers, and the two concepts drifted apart.

Astrology is the belief that the position of celestial bodies influences people’s lives. Astronomy is the scientific study of these bodies; it’s mathematics, using systems of calculations to predict where planets have been and where they will be, Jason Wright, a professor of astronomy and astrophysics, said.

“Over the decades, you see the planets move through all of the constellations of the zodiac,” Wright said.

Those patterns, tracked over centuries, became the basis for astrology. Horoscopes, Wright said, were based on the motions of the planets.

Many have continued using interpretations of celestial cycles based on solar calendars as a tool for insight on one’s personal life, but it used to be less inclusionary.

“Early astronomers like (Johannes) Kepler were given wages to be an astronomer, and to have the patronage of wealthy people and royalty by astrology,” Wright said.

Astrology has since evolved from being a service exclusively for the wealthy, largely due to a newspaper column publication by astrologer R.H Naylor in the 1930s. Today, horoscopes have remained a popular fixture of newspapers.

As such, people popularly analyze their birth charts, mapping out where the planets were at the time they were born. The horoscope hashtag on TikTok has approximately 2.1 million posts; on Instagram, 7.7 million.

A more practical use of astronomy was the creation of the calendar. Each zodiac season, a new constellation appears behind it, and each cycle makes up the 12 seasons of the zodiac.

But Kevin Luhman, a professor of astronomy and astrophysics, said axial precession creates inconsistencies between earth's calendar and the ecliptic path on which the sun is located.

Luhman said a person’s zodiac sign traditionally reflects which constellation the sun appeared in front of at the time of their birth. For example, he said, the sun was in front of the constellation of Sagittarius for a person born a Sagittarius.

This system was set up by the Babylonians in 500 B.C.E. But because of the way Earth’s axis has since shifted, the sun is no longer in front of the zodiac traditionally assigned to it.

“Today, if you're born at that time of year, the sun is not in front of the Sagittarius,” Luhman said. “By studying the history of astronomy, one can learn a lot about the origin of astrology as well.”

Nahks Tr'Ehnl, an instructional technology specialist within the department of astronomy and astrophysics, said with modern astronomical understanding, astrology has been a practice “left behind in astronomy.”

He said that over thousands of years, scientists have refined instruments to aid physics and mathematical systems so each generation understands things in a way nobody has before.

“Sometimes folks will have the belief, before taking an astronomy course, that Earth is the center of the universe,” Tr'Ehnl said. “Once you've taken the astronomy course, you know the Earth is actually just this one little, tiny rock orbiting a pretty ordinary star somewhere in the galaxy.”

He said the “you're-really-not-special-at-all” feeling that arises from such a realization is a common one. The manifestation of mythical, magical characteristics in astrology, he said, can be accredited to the human perspective of being fascinated with the cosmos.

“Humans are special in the sense that we're the first living creatures — that we know about — that understands the right to choose what they want to believe,” Tr'Ehnl said.

title: Off the record | Sociable Sarah
author: Miss Behave I The Daily Collegian
description:
Editor’s Note: Off the record is a weekly column written by a fourth-year Collegian staffer under an alias. It aims to promote a space for honest conversations about love, sex and relationships. Those interested in sharing their experiences or submitting a topic can do so through this anonymous form.

Dear Sarah,

Senior year is filled with so many final moments. Final first day of school. Final football game. Final late night with your girlfriends.

While I’m sure you recognize that male validation shouldn’t make or break your big senior year, it shouldn’t be a driving force in your life right now. Don’t think your year is a bust if you don’t leave with a boyfriend. You would be crushed if you spent the year pining for someone who couldn’t care less if you lived or died, or better yet, pursued someone who “isn’t ready” for anything.

Luckily for you, I have the perfect solution for all this yearning. Instead of yearning for a rom-com-type love, pour all that love into the people who have been there for you through everything — your girlfriends. They’re there for you when romantic love fails; they pick up all the pieces and then force you to eat your weight in ice cream.

There’s never going to be another time in your life when all your friends are a walk away, or you’re staying up until 3 a.m. laughing about all the dumb decisions you’ve made the day prior.

The relationships you should be preserving are the ones you already have, rather than withering away in a nonstop search for something more. I promise boyfriends aren’t as fulfilling as they may sound. College is where you find your bridesmaids, not your husband!

I understand people can balance a romantic partner and their friends seamlessly, but why take the chance and ruin a good thing? It’s a tale as old as time: girl has amazing friends, girl meets boyfriend, girl spends a lot of time with said boy, girl loses friends because they’re fed up with her constantly ditching them. Why let this be you when you can stay on that first chapter, the girl who has amazing friends?

In your final year, you have a lot on your plate: internships, jobs, graduation, and you don’t need a man who can’t be bothered added to the mix. Your girlfriends are the perfect combination of low stakes and low commitment. They get that some days you're going to respond to their message five hours later, and sometimes you’re not in the mood to bar crawl on a random Wednesday night. They know you love them and don’t have to prove it every minute of every day for it to be true.

You have your whole life to date crappy men, but you won’t always have your girlfriends there to debrief Sunday morning over an iced latte and Irving’s bagel. I’m drooling just thinking about it.

The truth is that I’ve been on dates, counting down the minutes until I could go back home and see my friends. The men were fine, but there’s something so special about my girls. I would be out with him, wishing I were with them.

One time, I canceled on him because my girls were getting triple dippers from Chili's in Altoona. I’m a girl with amazing friends and priorities.

Your senior year isn’t the time to get your heart broken. It’ll throw off the vibes for a while, and you’ll be kicking yourself that you let a loser ruin your plans.

We’ve all heard the stories about the couples who meet in college, get married, blah blah blah. Maybe your senior year feels like a last-ditch effort to secure that picture-perfect fairytale ending, but college isn’t the only place where you’ll meet a relationship-worthy partner.

You should be having fun, drinking (if you're of age, of course), partying and ever so occasionally studying.

I’m kidding. Please make sure you graduate.

I want you to have the best senior year imaginable, boyfriend or not. But let’s be real — preferably not. I have a strong feeling that when you’re crossing the stage, you’ll be thankful you spent time with your friends instead of the guy who claims he can’t do long-distance.

Until next time,

Miss Behave

title: Way-too-early season predictions for Penn State women’s basketball
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
It’s a new era of Penn State women’s basketball, with Tanisha Wright leading the charge since being hired in March.

Along the way, she’s recruited a team of nine athletes, which was much needed after every player hit the transfer portal from the year before.

With the new start and new team comes a lot of unanswered questions on how the team will compete this year. Who will be the leading scorers and go-to players? Will this team have what it takes to compete in the Big Ten?

Here are some way-too-early predictions for the Lady Lions’ 2026-27 campaign, which is now less than 100 days away.

Kamrah Banks will be top-3 team scorer

Despite being a freshman, Kamrah Banks has one of the highest ceilings for anyone on the team this year.

The 4-star guard graduated from Crispus Attucks High School in Indianapolis, where she left her mark with several school records. Among them was the all-time leading scorer and most points in a single game — a record previously held by NBA Hall of Famer Oscar Robertson.

While freshmen haven’t seen astronomical minutes in recent years for the Lady Lions, this year’s squad is much different. No one is as dominant as Gracie Merkle or Kiyomi McMiller and many spots in the starting lineup are likely up for grabs.

I believe Banks has the capability to be a starter early on. She may not get the nod in the first game due to her lack of collegiate experience, but the buzz surrounding her, coupled with whatever she can do off the bench, should earn her a starting role before the conference slate.

Even off the bench, I’d expect her to be one of the more dominant scorers on Penn State. She averaged 20.4 points per game her senior year and 26.4 points her junior year and has proven to be a capable offensive weapon.

Lady Lions will lose at least 1 ‘should-win’ games

Penn State has nine players on its roster who’ve never played together. No matter the number of summer workouts and fall practices, you can’t recreate in-game scenarios until it’s gametime.

The Lady Lions’ nonconference schedule hasn’t been released yet, but often opens with several Group of Six programs, including Bucknell, Cincinnati and Coppin State last season.

While these should result in wins for the Lady Lions, or any Big Ten team for that matter, the lack of chemistry could create issues early in the season.

I don’t expect the blue and white to come out of the nonconference stretch with a losing record, but I wouldn’t be surprised if it has a few losses to its name, even against an opponent it should beat.

Penn State will run 4 guard offense

With just nine players on its roster, Penn State doesn’t have much depth anywhere. However, the Lady Lions only have three forwards, giving very little relief to whoever makes the starting lineup.

Petra Božan and Cristen Carter are both experienced post players who will likely battle it out for a starting role, with the other coming off the bench with a large role. Freshman Irene García offers another player at forward, but was both a late addition to the team and someone with limited experience — likely giving her a very minimal role.

Instead, Penn State’s six guards offer many years of collegiate experience and will likely take up a large part of the starting five.

Between junior Devyn Quigley and graduate student Enjulina Gonzalez, the Lady Lions have experience in the guard room. With sophomores Ava Black and Skylar Durley, and freshmen Banks and Ashlee Brown, there’s enough depth to run a four guard, one forward lineup.

title: Report: Former Penn State player Jalen Pickett agrees to two-way deal with Los Angeles Clippers
author: Will Horstman | The Daily Collegian
description:
After entering NBA free agency just over a month ago, guard Jalen Pickett has found his next team.

Pickett and the Los Angeles Clippers have agreed to a two-way deal, according to Michael Scotto of Hoops Hype. The contract will allow Pickett to split time between the Clippers and their G League affiliate, the San Diego Clippers.

Pickett spent the past three seasons with the Denver Nuggets, who declined his team option earlier this summer, making him an unrestricted free agent. Pickett played in 50 games during the 2025-26 season, averaging 5.2 points per game.

This past season included a career-high night for Pickett, who scored 29 points during a win over the Philadelphia 76ers in January. Pickett started 18 games last season as he was a key depth piece when the Nuggets were facing injuries in their usual starting lineup.

Pickett was selected with the 32nd overall pick in the second round of the 2023 NBA draft by the Indiana Pacers, who traded his draft rights to Denver. Pickett played in 126 games with the Nuggets, averaging 4.0 points, 1.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game.

Prior to his NBA career, Pickett became a second-team All-American with Penn State in 2022-23, leading the Nittany Lions to the second round of the NCAA Tournament. He averaged 17.7 points, 7.4 rebounds and 6.6 assists per game during his memorable campaign.

Now, as Pickett starts the next step in his NBA journey, he'll get to be teammates with former Penn State player Yanic Konan Niederhauser on the Clippers.

author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Two more Nittany Lions have landed on an award watch list.

Tight ends Benjamin Brahmer and Gabe Burkle have been named to the John Mackey Award watch list, recognizing the top tight end in the country.

title: 3 overlooked Penn State position groups heading into 2026 season
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Heading into the 2026 season, conversations about Penn State have been dominated by Rocco Becht’s return from injury, the running backs battling for reps and the continued success of one of the nation’s most prestigious linebacker rooms.

But there are other position groups flying under the radar for a range of reasons. Some positions don’t get talked about while others are overshadowed by the major headlines.

Some of those overlooked position groups are crucial to the overall success of the team, so here are three that aren’t being talked about enough.

Cornerback

Daryus Dixson, Audavion Collins and Zion Tracy at the nickel haven’t been discussed nearly as much as the rest of the defensive backfield.

With Tony Rojas and Jeremiah Cooper returning from injuries, a lot of focus is being put on how well they’ll perform. However, the cornerbacks can unlock the full potential of D’Anton Lynn’s scheme.

If the cornerbacks perform up to standard, the Nittany Lions can put more emphasis on the blitz without worrying about getting torched by the opponent’s deep ball. But if the cornerbacks fall short of expectations, more pressure is put on the linebackers and safeties to compensate for a lack of confidence after missed assignments.

On paper, this room has the experience required to improve from last season, with all three having returned to continue playing under Terry Smith. It becomes a matter of them smoothly operating under Lynn’s defensive scheme, in tandem with Smith’s current and prior coaching strategies.

IOL

The offensive tackles have received a lot of attention this offseason. One spot is held by two-year starter Anthony Donkoh, and the other position covering Becht’s blind side is up for grabs.

However, Penn State needs the interior linemen to perform at their best for the entire offensive system to come together.

Trevor Buhr, Brock Riker and Cooper Cousins are the current projected starters. Riker was the starting center at Texas State and was named a Second Team Freshman All-American by The Athletic, while Buhr and Cousins have experience from Iowa State and Penn State, respectively, and are projected to break out this season.

Cousins has been a consistent face on Penn State’s line for the past two years and is ready to make a big leap as a full-time starter. Buhr has already played under Mouser’s offensive scheme and Ryan Clanton’s coaching, offering first-hand experience blocking for Carson Hansen.

Riker impressed the coaching staff throughout the offseason, earning high praise from Clanton as “the best center in the world.” He took advantage of the spring practices while Dominic Rulli was out with an injury, continuing to put on weight and take first-team reps.

Penn State’s interior is experienced and primed to come together for a great first season playing together for the Nittany Lions.

Kicker

The kicker is an underappreciated position group in football as it stands, often only noticed when mistakes are made or when games come down to the wire. However, the kicker is also the most reliable way to score points, and pairing a consistent leg with a strong defense could be Penn State’s way of slowly chipping away at opponents.

In an offensive system that doesn’t know where it stands among the Big Ten, Ryan Barker’s influence may be the safety net the Nittany Lions need.

Barker established himself as one of college football’s premier kickers last season when he broke Penn State’s single-season record for field goal percentage with 94.7%. As an incoming redshirt junior, he’s made 33 total field goals and is 92-for-94 on extra point attempts.

Close games are often decided by the final drive, and Barker isn’t a stranger to clutch situations. In his redshirt freshman season, Barker scored Penn State’s first first game-winning field goal since 2014, a 36-yard strike to beat USC on the road in overtime.

title: Preview | Penn State women’s soccer 2026 schedule full of rivalries, rematches
author: Mashiah Mitchell | For the Collegian
description:
The beginning of the fall semester brings the subsequent kickoff of the 2026 season for coach Erica Dambach’s Nittany Lions.

Dambach and her team have not seen a national championship since their one and only in 2015. They’ll likely be looking to work back to that level after a lackluster 2025 campaign that ended with their worst record under her leadership since 2010.

Despite the record, the Nittany Lions still returned to the NCAA tournament for the 32nd consecutive season, though it would be a short stint, with the squad losing in the second round to the University of Virginia.

This year’s 17-game schedule for the Nittany Lions is filled with conference contenders along with a few fresh opponents, including a first-time, never-before-seen nonconference meeting. Renewed rivalries, rematches and consistency is the name of the game for this year’s Nittany Lions.

The Nittany Lions will open their season on the road with back-to-back games against two teams that also made the NCAA tournament the previous season.

First, they’ll face the Notre Dame Fighting Irish on Aug. 16, a team that Dambach has never played and a team the Nittany Lions have not faced off against since 2006.

The Fighting Irish will return two of their three All-Americans in Izzy Engle and Annabelle Chukwu.

Then, they’ll take on the West Virginia Mountaineers on Aug. 20, who faced off against the Nittany Lions in their only away loss during the 2025 season.

Erica Dambach will also meet one of the greatest women’s coaches to ever grace the pitch, Nikki Izzo-Brown, who is entering her 30th season as the coach of the Mountaineers while looking to continue moving up the all-time wins list, now sitting at 425.

Then, the team will start a three-game homestand at Jeffrey Field in nonconference play, including the home opener against the Bucknell Bison on Aug. 27 and a first-time meeting with the Ivy League’s Brown University on Aug. 30.

The Nittany Lions will conclude non-conference play against a retooled Virginia Tech Hokies team that has seven incoming transfers on Sep. 3 before heading back on the road.

After that homestand is when the Nittany Lions’ season will begin picking up, with 12 straight Big Ten conference games and matchups against the defending Big Ten champions and runner-up.

The Big Ten slate starts in Columbus, Ohio, on Sep. 10 against a seasoned Ohio State Buckeyes team that has nearly ten returning seniors. It’s another rematch from last season for the Nittany Lions, one that resulted in a 2-0 win.

A familiar face will return to State College on Sep. 13, when the Nittany Lions play host to the Minnesota Golden Gophers. Former Penn State midfielder Keegan Schmeiser will make her first appearance in a different jersey since her 2024 transfer.

Another trip to the DMV is to follow on Sep. 18 against the Maryland Terrapins. The Nittany Lions will look to replicate their 4-0 win from last season and continue asserting dominance over a team still fairly new to the Big Ten compared to some of the other programs in the conference.

Then, it’s back home for a few weeks for the Nittany Lions. They’ll first play host to the Iowa Hawkeyes on Sep. 24, a team that just recently brought in new head coach Dean Ward after the departure of longtime boss Dave Dilanni.

Ward showed promise at Xavier University, leading the Musketeers to 31 wins and their first Big East Conference championship since 2019 in his short but meaningful two-year tenure. The matchup could be a defining game for the Nittany Lions.

After Iowa, they’ll take on two teams looking to get back to their former selves in the USC Trojans, who will take Jeffrey Field on Sep. 27 and the Purdue Boilermakers on Oct. 3.

After a disappointing season, USC added No. 1 freshman goalkeeper Josie Biehl to anchor their defense, which could possibly present problems for this year’s Nittany Lions.

Both teams finished in the bottom half of the Big Ten standings in 2025, unforeseen for a program like the Trojans that have been a consistent mainstay in the NCAA tournament.

The road then leads the Nittany Lions to Eugene, Oregon, on Oct. 8 to face the Oregon Ducks. Oregon finished dead last in the Big Ten just a year ago, winning only one conference game, interestingly enough against the eventual conference champion Washington Huskies.

Though their 3-10-5 record may say otherwise, this Oregon team presented hardship for the Nittany Lions last year in a 2-2 draw that was the difference maker in Penn State’s Big Ten ranking.

Quite possibly the biggest test of the season for the Nittany Lions will come on Oct. 11, when they travel to Seattle to face the Washington Huskies.

The Huskies are coming off their best season in program history, winning both the Big Ten regular season and tournament championships. They also reached the Elite Eight of the NCAA tournament for the first time since 2010.

Penn State will return home to face the Rutgers Scarlet Knights in a rivalry matchup on Oct. 17. The Scarlet Knights have not gotten the best of the Nittany Lions since the 2021 season in a 1-2 upset.

One more road trip will await the Nittany Lions after that, as they travel to the Mitten State to meet both Michigan State on Oct. 22 and Michigan on Oct. 25.

The season will close on Oct. 30 at Jeffrey Field against the Indiana Hoosiers.

Last season’s Hoosiers team managed a 1-2 upset against the Nittany Lions late in the year. With nine new freshmen additions along with eight seniors, Indiana could be primed for a resurgence in the Big Ten after a surprising bottom five finish.

title: The newest additions to Penn State women’s hockey’s incoming class
author: Dominic Megats I The Daily Collegian
description:
In his ninth season as head coach, Jeff Kampersal took the Penn State women’s hockey program to a new level: The Frozen Four.

Though they lost eight core seniors after the season concluded, for the Nittany Lions, gain often follows loss. Kampersal welcomed ten newcomers to his squad this offseason, three of which being transfer players. Six forwards, two defenseman and two goalies are featured in the new class.

Take a look at the new players set to wear the blue and white.

Transfers

Ashley Kokavec, defenseman

Kokavec, a 5-foot-5 defenseman, transferred once before making her way to Happy Valley as she spent her freshman season at Maine before spending her next two at Vermont.

The Palm Beach, Florida, native is coming off a season where she led all defenseman in points at Vermont with 17. Kokavec finished tied for third among Hockey East defensemen in assists with 14.

Alanna Devlin, forward

The second transfer addition comes from Boston College. Devlin played her first two collegiate years as an Eagle. There, she tallied 18 total points in 59 games.

Before committing to Boston College, she played 220 total games for North America Hockey Academy totalling 200 points and served as captain in her senior season.

Savanna Muir, goalie

Muir makes her way to Penn State after spending two seasons with SUNY Cortland. Although she didn’t see any time in net for the team, the Elizabeth, Pennsylvania, native found production with the Bishop Kearney Selects, where she recorded six shutouts in 11 appearances, finishing with a 9-1 record as a starter.

Recruits

Kylie Amelkovich, forward

One of the more promising forward recruits coming to Happy Valley is Amelkovich. The Glenn Illyn, Illinois, native spent three seasons at St. Mary’s Prep before committing to Penn State. There, she scored 76 goals in 152 games, totalling 159 points. Additionally, she represented Team USA in the 2025 and 2026 IIHF U18 Women’s World Championship.

Sofia Ismael, forward

Another emerging young forward makes her way from up north. Ismael played three seasons with the Etobicoke Dolphins along with representing Team Canada at the IIHF U18 Women’s World Championship in both 2025 and 2026.

With the Dolphins, Ismael recorded 171 points in 125 games. She captured gold with Canada in 2025 after posting four points in six games.

Megan Hosman, defenseman

The only defenseman in the freshman class makes her way from The Loomis Chaffee School along with spending some time with the Mid Fairfield Stars. Hosman donned the “C” as she captained her team through her senior year at Loomis Chaffee.

She earned the New England Defender of the Year award for the second-straight season after recording 29 points in 28 games.

Kayla McCarthy, forward

McCarthy, a Pennsylvania native, spent six seasons with the Pittsburgh Penguins Elite. In her final season, she recorded 20 goals and 21 assists, finishing with 41 points in 57 games.

She qualified for the USA Hockey National Championship five times.

Sydney McIntosh, forward

The Langley, British Columbia, native is coming off a season with RINK Hockey Academy Kelowna where she recorded 39 points in 48 games.

McIntosh helped her team capture the 2026 CSSHL Championship title before making her way to Penn State. She tallied seven points in five games in the playoffs.

Lorelai Nelson, forward

Nelson joins the Nittany Lions after four impressive seasons at Edina High School. She posted 179 points in 151 games, netting 82 goals.

The Edina, Minnesota, native served as captain in her final season and became a finalist for the 2026 Ms. Hockey Award. In addition to that award, Nelson earned All-Conference honors throughout her four years in high school and earned All-State honors twice. She finished her time at Edina High School averaging 1.12 points per game.

Morgan Stickney, goalie

Stickney is the sole netminder recruit in the young class. Starting in 34 games, the Manhattan Beach, California, native earned a 1.28 goals against average and a .944 save percentage.

Her final stat line at St. Mary’s earned her a spot on Team USA at the IIHF U18 World Championship for the second-straight year. She went 2-0-0 with two shutouts.

title: Penn State baseball earns commitment from pitcher Aidan Brokenshire
author: Gavin Leonard | For the Collegian
description:
Class of 2028 prospect Aidan Brokenshire has committed to Penn State, he announced Tuesday via X.

The Catawissa, Pennsylvania native is a right-handed pitcher listed at 6-foot-3 and 200 pounds.

As a sophomore, Brokenshire was one of Mount Carmel Area High School’s most productive batters. He recorded 30 RBIs, 26 hits and 10 stolen bases in 21 games.

Brokenshire pairs his hitting ability with his talent as a pitcher. During that same season, he held a 2.06 ERA while walking 14 batters over 37.1 innings.

With Brokenshire's committment, the Nittany Lions have added yet another young pitcher to their 2028 recruiting class.

title: Penn State Softball promotes Adrianna Baggetta to associate head coach
author: Gavin Leonard | For the Collegian
description:
Penn State softball has promoted Adrianna Baggetta to associate head coach, the team announced Tuesday via X.

Baggetta has spent three seasons as both assistant coach and hitting coach. During her tenure, Penn State’s offense set single-season records for home runs, runs scored and RBIs.

Before arriving in Happy Valley, Baggetta served five seasons as the head coach at Emory University, where she notched a 91-61 record and led the Eagles to the 2019 NCAA Division III championship series.

She will enter her fourth season with the program in 2027.

title: Jennifer Green hired as new Penn State women's gymnastics head coach
author: Mashiah Mitchell | For the Collegian
description:
Following a 9-7 season that finished with a third-place regional championship finish, Penn State unexpectedly had to begin the search for their next head coach after the departure of nine-year coach Sarah Brown.

What came out of the search was the subsequent signing of the reigning Mountain West Coach of the Year, Jennifer Green.

Green is a former gymnast turned coach, having spent four years at LSU in the 1980s, amongst a plethora of other accomplishments.

Green will leave behind a highly-touted legacy at Air Force, having built a program that produced nothing but talent and accolades under her tutelage.

Under Green’s leadership, Air Force has become a mainstay within the sport. In the previous season, they had their first-ever national championship qualifier in program history, Maggie Slife.

In addition to her work at Air Force, she also had short stints at both the University of Iowa and the University of Missouri.

During her tenure with Iowa, Green earned Regional Assistant Coach of the Year honors as well as contributing to multiple top regional finishes.

Green will inherit a very talented group that has shown consistency and competitiveness, and will continue to grow with Green for years to come.

title: Council president says borough ‘close’ to Addison Court purchase as redevelopment talks continue
author: Jonathon Chiu | The Daily Collegian
description:
State College Borough Council President Evan Myers began Monday’s meeting announcing the borough was close to an agreement to purchase Addison Court from PrimeCore Properties, an effort to maintain its affordability for senior residents and residents with disabilities in downtown State College.

As negotiations are ongoing, Myers didn’t provide details; but he said any agreement produced from talks would be discussed in a public meeting as part of a regular council agenda.

The council also voted unanimously to schedule a public hearing for Sept. 9 to resume discussions of PrimeCore's request for a height limitation amendment to the 200 block of South Allen Street located next to Addison Court. The borough will provide an amendment draft to the Centre County Planning & Community Development office and the Centre Regional Planning Commission for comment prior to the public hearing.

PrimeCore, which took over ownership of Addison Court from Beaver Court Associates in May, plans to demolish the building for a mixed-use structure called Encore.

While PrimeCore CEO Ara Kervandjian said a preservation plan for Addison Court is currently being explored, construction of Encore would commence if attempts to restore the building’s status within the Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) program were unsuccessful.

Addison Court’s status within the LIHTC, meant to maintain affordability for its tenants, expired on Dec. 31, 2024.

Kervandjian previously indicated that PrimeCore would still pursue construction of Encore should the amendment request be rejected.

The height limitations, set by borough ordinance 1597, are 65 feet. According to rationale for the amendment, part of the council’s April 20 agenda, PrimeCore argued the limitations prevent Encore from matching the appearance of Pugh Centre next door, another PrimeCore apartment development. It said this prevents it from pursuing its original plan of a “uniform 7-story 72-foot-high building.”

The planning commission voted 3-2 during its June 18 meeting to recommend the council reject the request.

title: SEE IT: Penn State wrestling visits White House to recognize 2026 National Championship
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
The Nittany Lions made a visit to the White House.

Following its 2026 National Championship victory, Penn State wrestling took a trip to Washington, D.C., to be recognized by President Donald Trump.

The Nittany Lions received an invite to the White House, as customary across many professional and collegiate sport champions in the country. The team posed for a picture in front of the White House with Trump and other local and federal officials to commemorate the season.

On Monday, the team visited the Pentagon where they were joined by alum and current UFC fighter Bo Nickal while meeting with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and sparring with military members.

Penn State dominated to a fifth straight national title, earning four individual national champions along the way. To cap off the season, Cael Sanderson and company were recognized at the White House for their title victory.

author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
The college football world is keeping a close eye on yet another Nittany Lion.

Blaise Sokach-Minnick was named to the Mannelly Award watch list, an annual award given to the nation's top long snapper.

A rising redshirt senior, Sokach-Minnick has seen action in six games thus far in his career, including two in each season from 2023-25. He is expected to be the team's starter aftering sitting behind Tyler Duzansky, who was named a finalist for the Mannelly Award last year.

If Sokach-Minnick goes the distance, he'll join Duzansky and Chris Stoll as the third finalist for the award in five years. Should he win the award, he'd follow in Stoll's footsteps as the second Penn State long snapper to earn the honor.

author: Mashiah Mitchell | For the Collegian
description:

Boston drafted Stecker in the third round of the 2026 PWHL draft with the No. 27 overall pick, following her four-year stint as a Nittany Lion and a career year in 2025.

Stecker was essential to the Nittany Lions’ Frozen Four berth last year, hitting career highs in assists, points, shots and plus/minus.

In addition to her offensive improvements, she was one of the biggest defensive anchors for the Nittany Lions not only last year, but all four years of her tenure, with more than over 80 career blocks.

Stecker showed promise and leadership across her Penn State career, and that will more than likely translate over into the pros.

title: Penn State QB Rocco Becht named to Maxwell Award watch list
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
Ahead of the 2026 season, the hype is growing around Rocco Becht.

Becht was named to the Maxwell Award watch list on Monday, given annually to the best all-around player in college football.

He was also named to the watch list in 2025 before the award was given to Indiana national championship-winning quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza. The last Nittany Lion to win the honor was running back Larry Johnson in 2002.

Becht is the winningest quarterback to return to college football. The gunslinger threw for 2,584 yards and 16 touchdowns last season in 12 games.

Becht recovered from a partially torn labrum throughout the spring and is slated to start under center for Penn State in Week 1.

title: State Theatre events from Aug. 3 through Aug. 9
author: Jackson Malenke | The Daily Collegian
description:
Another week, another set of movies flashing across The State Theatre’s screen and live music on its stage.

Here’s what you can catch this week.

Wednesday, August 5

“How to Train Your Dragon”

The State Theatre’s partnership with Schlow Library is continuing to bring children's movies to the screen on Wednesdays. This week’s film is the animated comedy “How to Train Your Dragon.”

The movie follows Hiccup — a boy who can’t kill a dragon in a land full of dragon slayers — who must find his way and come into his own.

The screening is in The Friedman Auditorium at noon, and it’s free with registration.

Thursday, August 6

Mad Dogs and Englishmen

This live concert experience celebrates Joe Cocker’s live album “Mad Dogs and Englishmen,” and tour of the same name.

This event includes all songs from the tour, not just those on the album, and will feature guests and a full choir.

It will be in the Friedman Auditorium at 8 p.m. for $55.46.

Friday, August 7

“Maytag Virgin”

The State Theatre is bringing a play to the stage this summer, with “Maytag Virgin.”

The play, directed by Jason Zanitsch, is a romantic comedy about two people facing complex loss and fear.

This event is in The Attic at 7:30 p.m., and it will cost $31.20 per ticket. This week's showings are also on Aug. 8 at 7:30 p.m. and Aug. 9 at 3 p.m.

“Risky Business”

The State Theatre is bringing another classic to the screen, this time starring Tom Cruise.

The film “Risky Business” follows a high school student whose parents leave town, and he decides to have some fun. Chaos ensues after he crashes his father’s car and he has to quickly come up with a lot of cash.

It can be seen in the Friedman Auditorium at 8 p.m. for $12.68 or $10.58 for students, sold online and at the door.

Saturday, August 8

“Do the Right Thing”

This critically acclaimed film from director Spike Lee follows an ensemble on the hottest day of the year in Brooklyn, New York.

The movie will be shown in the Friedman Auditorium at 8 p.m. Tickets are $12.68, or $10.58 for students, sold online and at the door.

Sunday, August 9

“Whisper of the Heart”

To end the week, the State Theatre is bringing a Studio Ghibli classic to the screen.

This film follows a magical cat and young girl who go on an adventure beyond their imaginations.

It’ll be in the Friedman Auditorium at 7:30 p.m. for $12.68 or $10.58 for students, sold online and at the door.

title: Penn State men's hockey earns commitment from defenseman Kohyn Eshkawogen
author: Rafael Rivera | For the Collegian
description:
2008-born defenseman Kohyn Eshkawogan has committed to Penn State, he announced on Instagram Saturday.

Eshkawogan, a Little Current, Ontario, native, registered 8 goals and 45 assists in 68 games this season with for the OHL’s Ottawa 67’s. Eshkawogan has been a key player for Ottawa, and one of the best defensemen in the league, leading him to be named to the OHL First All-Rookie Team.

The 17-year-old is considered a top prospect with potential to be selected in the first round of the 2027 NHL draft, and could bring an immediate impact to the Blue and White in the 27-28 season.

In his commitment post on Instagram, Eshkawogan emphasized his appreciation for the opportunity to play in Happy Valley.

“This is a big step in my journey, and I feel very fortunate for everyone who has helped me get here," Eshkawogan wrote. "I want to thank my family, my coaches, my teammates, and the Ottawa 67’s organization for their support and belief in me every day.”
